Treat "likely-relevant recent bug reports" as secondary evidence: they may or may not be relevant. Use them only if they help; otherwise, you may ignore them.

Some identifiers in the current bug report may be anonymized with placeholders (e.g., C#.M#). If the same token (e.g., C1) appears multiple times, it consistently refers to the same class (C) or method (M) throughout the report. These tokens are not complete qualified names. Title: Diagnosis
Details: The corresponding issue report describes that tooltip text in the UI is displayed with HTML entities such as " instead of the intended characters. This strongly suggests a missing escaping or decoding step in tooltip generation. Inspecting the implementation of StandardToolTipTagFragmentGenerator.generateToolTipFragment reveals that it directly returns the toolTipText without applying any escaping. Recent issue reports mention similar encoding or escaping problems in related UI components, reinforcing the suspicion that this method lacks proper handling. The behavior observed in the code matches the issue report's symptoms, indicating that missing escaping in this method is the likely root cause.

After providing this diagnosis, you will be prompted to suggest which methods would be the best locations to be fixed. The answers should be in the form of `ClassName.MethodName(ArgType1, ArgType2, ...)` without commentary (one per line), as your answer will be automatically processed before finally being presented to the user.

Title: Diagnosis
Details: The test `testNodeSetOperations` checks XPath binary operations involving node-sets, specifically an expression like "$array > 0". According to the current bug report, the issue is that binary operators involving node-sets do not behave according to the XPath specification. The spec states that if both operands are node-sets, the comparison is true if there is some pair of nodes (one from each node-set) whose string-values satisfy the comparison. Similarly, if one operand is a node-set and the other is a number, the comparison should evaluate by comparing the string-values of the node-set's nodes to the number according to XPath rules.

The key class likely implicated is `CoreOperation` in `org.apache.commons.jxpath.ri.compiler`. However, the method `evaluate` or similar evaluate methods in `CoreOperation` are not visible or easily retrieved, so direct inspection wasn't possible with the retrieved snippets.

The failure is presumably due to `CoreOperation` incorrectly implementing binary operations on node-sets, not following the specification that the operation should be a pairwise comparison of nodes' string values (or their numeric conversions). This results in logical comparisons failing or returning wrong results as tested by `testNodeSetOperations`.

Recent bug reports do not touch on this issue and relate more to other problems such as string trimming or reserved keywords, so they are not relevant here.

In summary, the root cause is that the `CoreOperation` class's implementation for binary operations does not properly handle cases where one or both operands are node-sets, violating XPath specifications. The test fails because the actual evaluation does not produce the correct Boolean outcomes expected by XPath rules.

Suggested fix locations are the methods in `CoreOperation` responsible for evaluating or handling binary operations on expressions that can be node-sets or numbers.

Based on the available information, provide the signatures of the most likely culprit methods for the bug. Your answer will be processed automatically, so make sure to only answer with the accurate signatures of all likely culprits (in `ClassName.MethodName(ArgType1, ArgType2, ...)` format), without commentary (one per line).
